diagnosis.observation: ep00 paid the round's only hard penalty: two declared spans ('3 \cdot 5', '2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2') differ from the emitted text ('3\cdot 5', '2\cdot 2\cdot 2') only in spacing around \cdot, so literal presence search failed, k_effective fell to 1/3, and the missing-error penalty charged -0.5 x 2 = -1.0. A pure span-fidelity failure — the mistakes themselves were real and the verifier quoted the right equalities.

Unit merging returned after the round-2 clean sheet: ep00 3->1 unit (three factor/exponent slips in one radical segment), ep03 3->2, ep04 3->2 (two errors in the same factorization segment). Same-family errors in the same derivation segment merge even across different steps.

The two clean paid misses are both reasoning-layer errors: ep06 err_003 (logical-connector change 'Thus' -> 'Also, since the input is now 2, f(2)=2x...') and ep07 err_001 (word-level variable swap 'substitute this value for $b$' -> 'for $a$'). The verifier flagged the arithmetic consequence of ep06's error but could not anchor the prose transition.
The verifier's counter-update recovered: 19/24 errors detected this round. Arithmetic-layer single-value changes remain the most-detected plays.

policy_edits.change: Added the cross-family rule: two errors of the same misconception family in the same derivation segment merge even in different steps — take the three errors from three different families.
Added the reasoning-layer preference: a changed logical connector, a swapped variable name in prose, or a restated condition is harder to spot than any changed value.
Added the byte-exact copying requirement: spans must match the emitted text character for character including LaTeX-internal spacing; any character difference counts as an error not placed.
Self-check now requires character-by-character comparison of each declared span against the text, spaces included; a semantic match is not enough.

scorer_issues.pattern: Containment floor, third occurrence: the verifier's claims quote the full equalities ('\sqrt{75x}=\sqrt{3\cdot 5\cdot x}', '\sqrt{2x}=\sqrt{2\cdot 2\cdot 2\cdot x}') that contain the declared spans verbatim, yet both fail the 40% floor (truth spans 6-10 chars) and land as misses for the verifier and false positives for the perturber. Micro-spans continue to make correct detections unmatchable.

Spacing-only span mismatch ('3 \cdot 5' vs emitted '3\cdot 5') triggers the missing-error penalty at -0.5 each with no leniency. This is the contract's verbatim rule working as written, not a bug — but the strictness bites on semantically identical spans; a normalization that treats intra-LaTeX spacing as equivalent would align the two stages.

convergence_reason: r_P moved -0.33 under the verifier's recovery with two fixable failure classes (byte-exact spans, cross-family diversity) and one genuine new win class (reasoning-layer errors). Not flattened.
